title: Matrix: Spiral Order
oneLiner: Walk a matrix clockwise from the outside in, keeping four boundaries and shrinking one after each edge.
keyTakeaway: Keep four boundaries, top, bottom, left and right. Read the top row left to right (then top++), the right column downwards (right--), the bottom row right to left (bottom--), the left column upwards (left++), and repeat while top <= bottom and left <= right. Re-check the bounds before the bottom row and left column, or a single leftover row or column is read twice.
explanation:
Return every element of an m by n matrix in spiral order: along the top row, down the right side, back along the bottom, up the left side, then the same again one ring further in. For [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6], [7, 8, 9]] the answer is [1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 8, 7, 4, 5].

Tracking a direction and turning when you hit a visited cell works, but needs a visited grid. The cleaner approach keeps four boundaries for the part not yet read: top = 0, bottom = m - 1, left = 0, right = n - 1. Each loop reads one ring in four legs, and after each leg moves that boundary inward: read row top from left to right, then top++. Read column right from top to bottom, then right--. Read row bottom from right to left, then bottom--. Read column left from bottom to top, then left++.

The trap is the last ring of a non-square matrix. For a single remaining row, the first leg reads it and top passes bottom; without a check, the third leg would read the same row backwards. So guard the third leg with if (top <= bottom) and the fourth with if (left <= right). Test [[1, 2, 3]] and [[1], [2], [3]] by hand; they catch this every time.

Every element is read exactly once: O(m · n) time and no extra space beyond the output. The same boundary bookkeeping builds a spiral (Spiral Matrix II) and shows up in grid problems that peel layers, like Rotate Image.

The visualization reads a 3 by 4 matrix; highlighted cells are the current leg, shaded ones are already read.

starterCode.python:
def spiral_order(matrix):
    result = []
    if not matrix:
        return result
    top, bottom, left, right = 0, len(matrix) - 1, 0, len(matrix[0]) - 1
    # TODO: while top <= bottom and left <= right:
    #   read row top (left to right), top += 1
    #   read column right (top to bottom), right -= 1
    #   if top <= bottom: read row bottom (right to left), bottom -= 1
    #   if left <= right: read column left (bottom to top), left += 1
    return result

visualizationSteps.message: Read a 3 by 4 matrix clockwise. Boundaries: top = 0, bottom = 2, left = 0, right = 3.
Top row 0, left to right, then top++: 1, 2, 3, 4. Output so far [1, 2, 3, 4]. Now top=1, bottom=2, left=0, right=3.
Right column 3, downwards, then right--: 8, 12. Output so far [1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 12]. Now top=1, bottom=2, left=0, right=2.
Bottom row 2, right to left, then bottom--: 11, 10, 9. Output so far [1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 12, 11, 10, 9]. Now top=1, bottom=1, left=0, right=2.
Left column 0, upwards, then left++: 5. Output so far [1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 12, 11, 10, 9, 5]. Now top=1, bottom=1, left=1, right=2.
Top row 1, left to right, then top++: 6, 7. Output so far [1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 12, 11, 10, 9, 5, 6, 7]. Now top=2, bottom=1, left=1, right=2.
The boundaries crossed, so every cell was read once: [1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 12, 11, 10, 9, 5, 6, 7].

recognitionSignals: "Spiral", "clockwise", "layer by layer" or "ring by ring" through a 2D grid.
A traversal order that changes direction at the edges of what is left.
gotchas: Without the top <= bottom and left <= right checks before the last two legs, a leftover single row or column is read twice.
An empty matrix ([]) has no first row; return [] before reading matrix[0].
Off by one on the corners: each leg starts where the previous one ended, after its boundary moved, so no corner is read twice.
confusableWith: Rotate Image also works ring by ring, but moves values between the four sides instead of reading them out.
Grid BFS (Number of Islands) visits by distance from a start cell; spiral order is a fixed geometric walk with no queue.

complexity.note: Each of the n · m cells is read exactly once. Apart from the output list (O(n · m) if you count it), only four boundary variables are stored.
